turns.speaker: Tony Fadell
turns.en: Look, I was building hardware when it wasn't in Vogue in 1995 and '96. Everyone's like, "Tony," and this was in the Valley, "Tony, you're crazy. It's all about the internet. We don't need any hardware." And then iPod comes, and I was pitching new businesses in '99 and 2000. They're like, "Well, that's the stupidest idea ever." Then the iPod comes out, "Tony, you want to leave Apple and start that business you wanted to do with hardware?" And then it was like, okay. Then it was all software mobile stuff again, like, " Okay, we don't need anything," but we can't get to the next level of software if we don't make the next level of hardware. And the revolution has to happen completely. You got to have the mobile network and the mobile network software for the mobile network to work. You had to have the MP3 player and the MP3 format bits to make that work. (01:14:23): We're seeing with AI, we got to have AI plus all the data centers and edge compute to make that work. And then over time, the hardware becomes less, it becomes more mundane. Okay, it doesn't change as much, but all the software starts to then... So I've always just been continually going through the things that I love to do and doing the things at the full stack level, because that's where I know is innovation, that's what we had to do at Nest. We had to innovate at the software level, the hardware level, the network level to get the first thermostat out and then the Nest Protect and all that stuff. If we look now, going on, people are like, if you're a SaaS company or if you're a software only company, your software companies' worthless because anyone can vibe code it into the thing. And then they're like, "We're only funding companies that have atoms in their business plan with software." I'm like, "Duh. Where have you guys been?" (01:15:22): So it's just funny to watch these cycles go and happen, and it's like, "Okay, all right, you guys can go chase your tails. I'm going to just keep here doing these full system kind of products and businesses." Yes, they're a lot harder, and yes, they cost more money, and yes, they're going to take longer to scale and adopt and blah, blah, blah, but they have staying power for years. And they bring new features that you could have never had if you just did software only because you need, especially, let's say, in robotics, you need new sensors and new this and new that and what have you. Look at Waymo, it's an electric car with tons of sensors and everything. It's a hardware platform. Maybe it doesn't look as streamlined as maybe a smartphone, but it's an incredible hardware platform with an incredible software platform. And that is something that we're going to be able to innovate on, and it'll become a platform for something else, I'm sure, delivery or this or whatever else.
turns.zh: 听着，我在1995年和1996年做硬件的时候，那可不是什么时髦的事。当时所有人都说：“托尼，”（这是在硅谷），“托尼，你疯了。现在全是互联网，我们不需要任何硬件。” 然后iPod问世了。1999年和2000年，我向人们推销新业务时，他们又说：“这真是最愚蠢的主意了。” 接着iPod上市了，“托尼，你想离开苹果去创办你想做的硬件业务？” 然后我就想，好吧。接着又全是移动软件相关的东西了，比如，“好吧，我们不需要任何东西。” 但如果不制造下一代硬件，我们就无法实现下一代软件的突破。整个变革必须彻底完成。你得有移动网络和移动网络软件，才能让移动网络正常运行。你还得有MP3播放器和MP3格式文件，才能实现这一目标。（01:14:23）：看看人工智能领域，我们必须拥有人工智能技术，再加上所有数据中心和边缘计算，才能让它发挥作用。而随着时间推移，硬件会变得越来越少见，越来越普通。好吧，它变化不大，但所有软件都开始……所以我一直不断地做着自己热爱的事情，在全栈层面进行创新，因为我知道这才是创新所在。这也是我们在Nest公司必须做的。我们必须在软件层面、硬件层面、网络层面进行创新，才能推出首款恒温器，然后是Nest Protect等产品。现在看看，人们会说，如果你是一家SaaS公司，或者纯软件公司，你的软件毫无价值，因为任何人都能把代码融入产品中。然后他们又说：“我们只资助那些商业计划中包含实体产品的公司。” 我就会说：“得了吧。你们这些人去忙活吧。” （01:15:22）：所以看着这些周期来来去去真的很有趣。就好像，“好吧，那好吧，你们去忙活吧。我就继续做这些全系统类型的产品和业务。” 是的，它们确实更难，也更费钱，而且上规模和普及需要更长时间等等，但它们能持续数年。它们能带来单纯做软件永远无法实现的新功能，因为你需要，尤其是比如说在机器人领域，你需要新的传感器和各种新东西。看看Waymo，那是一辆装满传感器的电动汽车。它是一个硬件平台。也许它看起来不像智能手机那么流畅，但它是一个令人惊叹的硬件平台，搭配着令人惊叹的软件平台。这正是我们将能够进行创新的领域，我相信它会成为其他领域的平台，比如配送服务或者其他什么。

You just see it, and you're like, okay, I was there at '99 when the bottom fell out, and AI is different, but there's a lot of similarities, and we're going to have the gen one companies, the gen two companies. And when people really understand product instead of selling technology platforms that people have to figure out for themselves. So it's fun to watch. It's a game.
turns.zh: 是啊，这真的很有意思。旧事物常有新意，我从事这行已经35、40年了。你看到某些现象时，会感慨道：好吧，我99年就经历过市场崩盘，那时和现在人工智能虽然不同，但也有很多相似之处。我们会看到第一代公司和第二代公司。当人们真正专注于产品本身，而不是把技术平台当作产品去推销时，那才是真正的乐趣。这就像一场游戏，值得关注。

And the workers hate doing inventory, counting everything on every shelf, and all that stuff. So it really works, and I love seeing that stuff. We're doing the same thing at Greyparrot with AI and recycling. It's literally figuring out what things should go in this recycling bin versus that and doing it really fast with cameras and all this stuff. (01:18:05): And we've been at that for a few years, and we have AI plus textiles. Most textiles have weaving errors, and color errors, and defects, and things like that. And so people still make all of these products, but then they have to incinerate them because they're not perfect at the end because they don't catch the quality problems early enough in the product. And we're doing AI plus cameras to spot all this stuff. And again, another thing. We've been doing AI and drug design now for 10 years at Orionis, and that's taking off. So I'm really interested in not just these frontier models, and this whole other thing is really good AI that you can trust, scoped correctly with this, solving real problems every day as opposed to pipe dream AGI, okay, you can go solve that. I'm going to go and build all these businesses that really matter right now. (01:19:01): And we're finally getting traction because people are like what AI and oh, more robotics and now, all of a sudden, we're in vogue, and we've been here really working on our product-market fit, working on our marketing, working on version 3.0 the device and everything, and people are adopting them. And that's what's wonderful to see. And so I'm excited by all that. We have another one like AI Infusion and doing that, or finally doing tons of software with chemical reactions, and now we have a clean agricultural fuel and oils company that is cleaning up farms all around Central America, and we're almost all atoms plus software in some way. And so it's just nice to be sitting here and knowing that we made these bets a long time ago and we're doing it. Now we're not necessarily... I was early on in Grok, and it was cheap then, and it was like, "Yeah, that's the right way to go." (01:20:07): And my friends were in Cerebras, and I got into that, and then it's like, but these are long-term plays, and they're finally coming to fruition, but we did invested in it not when it was hyped, and it's... We were doing it back when unicorns valuations were billions of dollars. Today, if you don't have a $5 billion round raised, you're not anything. It's like, okay, well, that doesn't work from a venture perspective. You never get their venture returns. You can't invest in things when the valuations are already nine digits or 10 digits, and you think you're got a small portfolio that's got like... Uh-uh, that's not the kind of game I want to play. So I'm glad that we are well positioned in all these companies that have real good product-market fit, that came in the right valuations, that we can really help and make big change and deliver painkillers, and we'll let everybody else over there play. So that's what's exciting to me.
turns.zh:
到现在为止，我一直在做人工智能与硬件相结合的项目——不只是在Nest公司，还有我们在Build大会上投资的许多初创公司。比如Simbe Robotics这样的公司。我们很早就开始做机器人技术，但现在做的不是人形机器人，而是用于零售商店库存盘点的设备。我们已经研究了八年，七年了，现在这个项目终于开始起步了。它确实运用了人工智能技术，搭建了机器人平台，切实解决了零售商在库存管理方面的痛点。员工们讨厌盘点库存、数每个货架上的商品之类的工作。所以这个项目确实有效，我很高兴看到这样的成果。

我们在Greyparrot公司也做了类似的项目，将人工智能与回收利用结合起来。具体来说，就是通过摄像头快速识别物品，判断它们应该归入哪个回收箱。这方面我们也研究了几年。还有人工智能与纺织品检测的结合。大多数纺织品都存在织物瑕疵、颜色偏差和质量缺陷等问题。尽管如此，人们还是会生产这些产品，但最后不得不焚毁，因为产品最终没有达到质量标准，无法提前发现问题。而我们用人工智能和摄像头技术来检测这些问题。另外，我们在Orionis公司进行人工智能药物设计已经十年了，这项技术也正在取得进展。

我对这些前沿应用很感兴趣，同时也对真正可靠、经过正确规划的AI技术感兴趣，它能每天解决实际问题，而不是空想的通用人工智能（AGI）。好吧，你可以去研究那些，但我现在更专注于真正重要的业务。（01:19:01）我们终于获得了关注，因为人们会问：“AI技术？哦，又是机器人技术。” 突然间，我们又成了热门话题。我们一直在优化产品与市场的适配，加强市场推广，开发第三代设备等等，现在人们开始采用我们的技术。这真是令人欣喜的成果。我对此充满热情。我们还有其他项目，比如AI Infusion，致力于将AI与化学反应相结合。如今，我们的清洁农业燃料和润滑油公司正在中美洲各地为农场提供清洁能源，我们基本上是在某种程度上将原子与软件相结合。能坐在这里，知道我们多年前就下了这些赌注，现在正在兑现承诺，真是太好了。（01:20:07）我很早就参与了Grok项目，当时它价格低廉，我当时就觉得：“没错，这才是正确的方向。” 我的朋友们投身于Cerebras项目，我也加入了进来。但这些都是长期投资，现在终于开始开花结果了。我们投资它们的时候，并不是在它们被炒作得火热的时候，而是早在独角兽估值达到数十亿美元的时候。如今，如果你没有筹集到50亿美元的融资，你就什么都不是了。从风投的角度来看，这太不划算了。你永远无法获得他们的回报。当估值已经达到9位数或10位数时，你再去投资小型投资组合，根本不划算。这不是我想参与的游戏。所以我很高兴我们在所有这些产品与市场适配良好的公司中占据有利地位，帮助它们实现重大变革，解决实际问题，让其他人去竞争。这才是让我兴奋的地方。

Feels like all the things are converging around the things that you have been doing for so long, and the technology is finally getting exactly as described to actually something amazing.
turns.zh: 天哪，我前几天在另一个播客上用过一句话，我觉得很适合你。这句话出自《圣经》："你生来就是为了迎接这样的时刻。"感觉所有事情都汇聚在一起，与你长期以来所做之事相契合，而科技终于如预期般发展出惊人的成果。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: For people that don't know what you do these days, you talked about all these companies you work with, help people understand what it is you spend your time on, in case they may want to try to work with you on this stuff.

turns.speaker: Tony Fadell
turns.en: I think the first thing to know is that we invest in deep technology. So that could be hardware, it could be software, software plus hardware, it could be chemical, it could be all kinds of different stuff. But remember, we talked earlier about what's the pain and is there new technology that comes out to solve that pain in a new way? And so what we do is I've learned that I invest in the deep technologies that are going to unseat the incumbents because it's going to change the market or the product in such a dramatic way that customers will choose this. So we're not just competing on features or better marketing or whatever. We're fundamentally a different product. Now it might take longer to get the market to shift to it, but it's fundamentally different, just like I brought up Grok and Cerebras and these kinds of things. (01:22:42): It's fundamentally different. And so at Build, what we do is we invest in those technology companies that can be that seed that can unseat things, and maybe they go the distance, or maybe they are the key enabling tech that allows another startup to go to the distance, that kind of stuff. And so that's what we invest in, and we do it in the environment, in societal benefits, and health benefits. That's where we focus, and at times we've had a portfolio of over 200 companies, and we do that, but we don't just invest. (01:23:16): When we get involved, many of the companies we advise and that we come in help them with product management, operations, we help them with financing, we help them with org development, just all kinds of different ways that... A lot of times in marketing and communications, right? Because we talked about storytelling, storytelling is really important, and a lot of deep technology people, they're incredible engineers, scientists, researchers, what have you. They have a really good idea, but they don't necessarily know how to form the product around it, or form the marketing around the product they're building, or help the marketing to inform the product and vice versa. (01:23:56): And so we try to encapsulate that and really bring that to bear so they don't hit it on the fourth version. They try to get very close to the first or second version so they can get on that three version cycle to get to a great company, and so that's what we do. So we get to have a lot of fun. We get to word play in all these different spaces: health, medicine, drugs, robotics, chips, these kinds of things. So that's just what's wonderful to us, and we get to just be kids in the candy store and work with all these incredible, smart entrepreneurs and everything. So that's one thing I do. The other thing I do is I'm a designer at residence at MIT. So I just finished up my first year there with the MIT Media Lab in architecture and design, and help to give lectures and work with students, amazing, amazing, smart students with the great technology, but help them with the customer journey. (01:25:01): Try to make sure that they see this stuff early on in their career, not after 10 years, and then they finally understand, oh, wait a second, what am I really building? Who is it for? Not just what is it am I building, but why am I building it, and for who? And so, trying to get that into some of the later undergraduate and graduate students so we can watch them change the world more quickly.
turns.zh:
我认为首先要了解的是，我们投资的是深度技术。这可能包括硬件、软件、软硬件结合、化学技术等各种领域。但请记住，我们之前讨论过：痛点是什么？是否有新技术能以新方式解决这些痛点？因此，我们的投资策略是，我发现那些能够颠覆现有市场或产品、以极具震撼力的方式让客户选择新技术的深度科技，才最有可能击败现有巨头。这意味着我们不只是在功能、营销或其他方面竞争，而是提供一种全新的产品。当然，让市场接受新技术可能需要更长时间，但这种产品本质上是颠覆性的。正如我提到的Grok、Cerebras等公司，它们都具有这种颠覆性。

在Build大会上，我们专注于投资那些能够引发变革的科技公司。这些公司或许能独自颠覆现有格局，或许成为其他初创公司的关键赋能技术。我们的投资方向聚焦于环境、社会效益和健康领域。我们曾管理超过200家投资组合公司，但投资并非唯一手段。当我们介入时，会为许多公司提供产品管理、运营、融资、组织发展等全方位支持——尤其是在市场营销和传播方面。比如讲故事能力至关重要，许多深度科技人才都是出色的工程师、科学家、研究人员，他们拥有卓越的技术洞察力，但不一定擅长围绕产品打造营销体系，或让营销反哺产品研发。我们的目标是帮助他们避免在第四版产品上折戟，尽早完成第一或第二版产品，从而开启三轮迭代，成就伟大企业。

这份工作充满乐趣。我们能在健康、医药、药物、机器人、芯片等领域尽情探索。最棒的是，能像孩子在糖果店般自由发挥，与这些才华横溢的创业者共事。这就是我的工作核心。另一个身份是麻省理工学院的驻校设计师。我刚在那里完成了第一年的学习，参与建筑与设计实验室的教学，帮助学生理解客户旅程，确保他们在职业生涯早期就能领悟产品核心价值——而不是十年后才恍然大悟：我到底在为谁构建这个产品？为什么要这样做？这正是我们致力于让晚期本科生和研究生更早领悟商业本质的初衷——助力他们更快改变世界。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Incredible. I love just all the levels of ways you are helping people. There's the investing, there's this book, there's MIT, there's these conversations.
turns.zh: 太不可思议了。我喜欢你帮助人们的各种方式——投资、写书、与麻省理工学院合作，还有这些对话。

turns.speaker: Tony Fadell
turns.en: It's fun. It's just so much fun.
turns.zh: 这真的很有趣。太有意思了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love how much fun you're having. Is there anything else you wanted to share that we didn't cover?
turns.zh: 我很欣赏你享受其中的乐趣。还有什么想和我们分享的但我们没聊到的吗？

turns.speaker: Tony Fadell
turns.en: We should really just talk about ethics and morals and your point of view on that. And as a product manager, as a product designer, you need to really consider these things. I understand we have lots of big questions about AI and is it going to be a disaster for the next generation and for societies and all the other stuff? But I think that you really need to be well grounded and have real principles when you're designing something, and don't let those things go astray, just like you wouldn't go astray with a bad user interface or something like that. Make sure you're not trying to addict your users. And if anybody is, there's always other jobs, and there's always other better companies, and don't chase the money for tearing apart what it is the fabric of this society that we built. Obviously, there's going to be innovation, and there's going to be change, but when you're really doing it, and you can see that you're doing it, and you're trying to get people hooked, or you're like, "Oh, I give more dopamine or what have you." (01:26:47): That's when you have to start really looking at things. And a lot of times, people are young, and they think, "Oh, that's great. That's what I want." But when you start to have kids, and you start to have families, and you start to see the... And you're not just about you; you're not trying to just get out of your family when you were growing up. I'm an individual, and I want what I want. You really need to start thinking systemically about the benefit that you're bringing to this society as a whole, not just to the business that you're in and trying to bring in whatever revenue you're trying to do because at the end of the day, users will feel that and then I think and will reward that as we see with Apple with privacy and people say, "Oh, they're behind because they're so private and there's this." (01:27:34): But it's a double-edged sword. I remember when we had a very pointed discussion when the iTunes music store and when it was turning into video was being specified and what we were thinking about it, and everyone's like, "Oh, this is going to be great. We're going to do movies. We're going to do TV shows. That's going to all be great. We're going to make a lot of money with this in the studios. Everybody's behind it." And then somebody goes, "Yeah, and we should have porn, of course." Steve was like, "What? Is that the kind of world you want your kids to grow up in? And Apple is related with that and Apple's about... Is that what we want to do?" And it was very clear, it was shut down, and we need leaders like that. We need leaders who are very clear as opposed to "I'm going to make a huge service for everyone." And they're all sex chatbots for everyone. (01:28:24): I just think when you start normalizing those things, and you start telling other generations that's a value and you start... And I understand that everyone has their own what's right and what's wrong. And here I am, the old guy, again, I think we can go a little too far. I'm for individual rights and for everyone to be a thing, but when major companies are doing this in the guise of certain kinds of behaviors they're trying to achieve, when we're selling... We're turning personal connection into a product with AI chatbots and making them really devolve social interaction to the point where I'm going to have a perfect interaction with this thing because the world is so messy, it's like we're losing humanity with that, and we're just for gain. So I wish that the other product designers out there really take it to heart. I'm not saying you got to be Lily White and being in a church every weekend and Bible banging. I'm not saying that; I'm not MAGA. I'm not any of that stuff, just saying, hey, think about it.
turns.zh:
咱们真的应该只谈论伦理和道德，以及你对此的看法。作为产品经理、产品设计师，你需要认真考虑这些问题。我知道我们对人工智能有很多疑问，比如它会不会给下一代和社会带来灾难之类的。但我认为，在设计产品时，你必须立足根本，坚守原则，不能偏离正轨，就像你不会在用户界面设计上走弯路一样。别试图让用户上瘾。如果有人这么做，总会有其他工作机会，总会有更好的公司。别为了金钱而撕裂我们所建立的社会结构。显然，创新和变革是必然的，但当你亲身参与其中时，当你意识到自己在试图让人们上瘾，或者你说“哦，我要增加多巴胺分泌之类的”时，那时候你就必须审视自己的行为了。很多时候，年轻人会想：“哦，太棒了，这就是我想要的。” 但当你有了孩子，有了家庭，你会开始看到更广阔的世界——你不再只为自己而活，不再试图逃离成长过程中的家庭束缚。我是个独立个体，我要追求自己想要的东西。但你真的需要从系统层面思考，你为整个社会带来的价值，而不只是为所在的企业创造收益。毕竟，用户最终会感受到这一点，并给予回报。比如苹果在隐私问题上的处理，人们会说：“他们落后了，因为他们太注重隐私了，所以才这样。” 但这是一把双刃剑。我记得当初我们在讨论iTunes音乐商店转向视频业务时，大家都兴奋不已，觉得能拍电影、拍电视剧，能让影视公司赚大钱，人人都支持。但有人说：“对啊，那我们就应该加入成人内容啊。” 史蒂夫当时说：“什么？你希望自己的孩子成长在这样的世界里吗？苹果与此相关吗？这就是我们想做的吗？” 当时这个讨论被果断叫停。我们需要这样的领导者——他们立场坚定，而不是高喊“我们要为所有人打造伟大服务”。结果却成了面向所有人的性聊天机器人。（01:28:24） 我认为，当你开始将这些行为常态化，向下一代宣扬这是价值观时，当你开始……我理解每个人都有自己的是非观。我这个老家伙再说一句，我觉得我们做得太过火了。我支持个人权利，支持每个人自由发展，但当大公司打着某些行为的幌子来实现目的，当我们把人际交往商品化，用AI聊天机器人把社交互动降格到“我和这个东西能完美互动”的程度时，当这个世界变得如此混乱时，我们正在失去人性，只为追逐利益。所以我希望其他产品设计师能真正用心领会。我不是在
别说你得成为个“完美圣人”，每个周末都泡在教堂里念经祷告。我可不是在宣扬这种观点，我也不认同“让美国再次伟大”的那套说辞。我对那些东西一点兴趣都没有，只是想说，嘿，别忘了反思一下自己。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: A lot of people look at the iPhone as this thing now that everyone's hooked on. It's so good. We're just like, it's too good. And there's all this data showing all the impact it has on people and things like that. Just how do you think about that and the impact the iPhone has had on people?
turns.zh: 很多人把iPhone视为如今人人都离不开的神器。它确实太棒了。我们总觉得它好得令人惊叹。各种数据也表明它对人们和社会产生了深远影响。但你如何看待iPhone对人们的影响呢？

turns.speaker: Tony Fadell
turns.en: Well, the first thing is the iPhone wasn't set out to be that. There's unintended consequences, and the unintended consequence was social media happened, and social media, Apple's not a social media company, but it does distribute the apps or make available those apps. And so the way I think about it is we have lots of junk food, and we have an obese nation or obese world because of all the junk food, and it takes us to regulate our consumption to do that and get healthy tools. And there's nutritional elements on the back of things. If you want to make a better decision, you can, and I hope AI and these assistants will help people be able to get better control of those kinds of things where our lizard brain is being stimulated in a way that consume more, consume more of physical food. And now the same thing's happening in digital food, but we have digital food that doesn't have the nutrition labels, doesn't have the warnings, doesn't have the regulation that it needs to have, just like we do with our physical food because, oh, you can't let innovation, whatever, be slowed down. (01:31:09): I'm not saying again, being a nanny and all the other stuff, but we got to have some balance, and it's just swung too far. And I still think that the platform companies like Google and Apple could be doing a lot more around digital consumption tools and information to help people make better decisions for themselves, for their families, and what have you, because you could go to the... iPhone's just a refrigerator, and you can put in junk food or you can put in good food. And even if you put in good food, you could go to the good food every five seconds. You have a refrigerator in your kitchen. You can put good food or bad food. (01:31:46): You could open it all the time and keep consuming. So we need to learn habits. We need to teach habits. We need to put in regulations. We need information. We need tools to help us monitor and manage that stuff, and they need to be supplied. And just like we have rules around who can buy something when they're 21 or under 21. We need all those kinds of things, and it needs to happen because why? Sure, you could have a short-term gaining of customers, but if you make your customers unhealthy, you're not going to have customers.
turns.zh: 首先，iPhone并非为此而设计。它带来了意想不到的后果——社交媒体的兴起。苹果并非社交媒体公司，但它确实分发或提供应用程序。因此，我的看法是，我们身边有很多“垃圾食品”，比如肥胖症患者之所以肥胖，正是因为这些“垃圾食品”。我们需要规范消费行为，采用健康工具。比如产品背面有营养标签。如果你想做出更好的选择，完全可以做到。我希望AI和语音助手能帮助人们更好地控制这些诱惑——就像我们的大脑被刺激去消费更多实体食品一样。如今数字食品领域也出现了同样的问题，但数字食品缺乏营养标签、警示信息和必要监管，正如实体食品有严格监管一样。毕竟，不能因为创新而拖慢脚步。（01:31:09）我不是说要当监管者，但我们必须找到平衡点，现在的趋势已经太过分了。我仍然认为谷歌和苹果这样的平台公司本可以为数字消费工具和信息提供更多帮助，帮助人们为自己、家人做出更明智的决策。毕竟iPhone就是个冰箱，你可以放进垃圾食品，也能放进健康食品。但即便放进健康食品，你也会每隔五分钟就去拿一次。厨房里的冰箱也是如此。你可以随时打开，不断消费。所以我们需要养成习惯，教会人们这些习惯，制定规则，提供信息和工具来监控和管理这些行为。就像限制21岁以下人群购买酒精饮料一样，这些措施都是必要的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Let me just say for folks that haven't read your book, I just want to communicate how great it is. There's very few books that are both tactically useful that give you, like, here's how to do a thing and also just inspire you to build and make great things. And Build does that in such a great way. I think everyone knows about it. I don't know if everyone's read it. So highly encourage you to read it. Two final questions. Where can folks find you online if they want to maybe learn about the stuff you're up to now, and how can listeners be useful to you?
turns.zh: 我想对没读过你书的人说，想说它太棒了。很少有书既实用又能激励你去创造和成就伟大事业。《Build》这本书就做得非常出色。我相信大家都知道这本书，但不确定是否都读过。所以强烈推荐大家读一读。最后两个问题。读者如果想了解你现在在做什么，可以在哪里找到你？听众如何能为你提供帮助？

turns.speaker: Tony Fadell
turns.en: Great. Well, let's see. Well, thanks again. This was a fun interview. I really enjoyed it. I think if you want to interact with us, we're at buildc.com. So Build Collective, but we're BuildC, B-U-I-L-D-C.com. You can go and see the companies we invest in, and you can find ways to contact us there. And how can viewers help me or help us? I think learn about the companies, see if you can model whatever you're doing in some of the learn from insights. There's a lot of websites that we help to create. A lot of the marketing we created for deep tech through those investments we made, so you can see some well done marketing. I hope you like our website for BuildC to show you how what we think is a really great website that only... Doesn't sell things necessarily. You know what I mean? Like point and click and purchase, but it just get them... Rebuild and apply it. (01:33:46): I think that's the most thing is: rebuild, read other things like that, and really hone your craft, make better products, make a better world because the world only gets better by the things we make and what we bring. And so, to me, that's the most important way to help me is by making other cool products like Flighty or other things. They're like, "I love this thing." So make great stuff, people, and don't think the AIs will. Use them for the tools that they can help with, but don't have cognitive surrender. Don't surrender to the machine. We can use the machines, but don't cognitively surrender and make better stuff. Make better stuff than myself or any of the teams that we back can make because we do have better tools now. So please do.
turns.zh: 太棒了。好吧，让我看看。嗯，再次感谢。这次采访真的很有趣。我觉得如果你们想和我们互动，可以访问buildc.com。就是Build Collective，但我们用的是BuildC，B-U-I-L-D-C.com。你们可以在那里查看我们投资的公司，也能找到联系我们的方式。观众们如何能帮助我或我们呢？我觉得可以了解这些公司，看看能否借鉴你们正在做的事情，从这些见解中学习。还有很多我们帮助创建的网站。通过这些投资，我们为深度科技领域做了很多营销工作，所以你们能看到一些优秀的营销案例。我希望你们能喜欢BuildC的网站，向你们展示我们认为非常出色的网站——它不一定是那种直接销售商品的……你们懂我的意思吧？比如点击购买之类的，但我们只是希望人们……重新构建并应用这些知识。（01:33:46）：我认为最重要的是：重新构建，阅读相关内容，真正磨练自己的技能，打造更好的产品，创造更美好的世界，因为世界只有通过我们创造和贡献才能变得更好。所以对我来说，帮助我的最重要方式就是创造像Flighty这样的优秀产品，或者其他类似的东西。他们会说：“我太喜欢这个产品了。” 所以，请大家创造出色的产品，别把希望寄托在人工智能上。利用人工智能能提供的工具，但别在认知上屈服。别向机器屈服。我们可以利用这些工具，但别在认知上妥协，创造出比我们自己或我们支持的团队更出色的产品，因为我们现在确实拥有更好的工具了。所以，请务必这样做。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. Tony, thank you so much for being here.
turns.zh: 太棒了。托尼，非常感谢你能来。

turns.speaker: Tony Fadell
turns.en: Hey, Lenny, that was great. Really appreciate it. Looking forward to seeing what your audience creates.
turns.zh: 嘿，莱尼，太棒了。真的很感激。期待看到你的听众们创造出什么成果。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Same. Bye, everyone. Thank you so much for listening. You can find all past episodes or learn more about the show at lennyspodcast.com. See you in the next episode.
turns.zh: 我也是。再见了，各位。非常感谢你们的收听。如果觉得这期节目有价值，可以在Apple Podcasts、Spotify或你喜欢的播客应用上订阅。也欢迎给我们评分或写评论，这对其他听众找到播客很有帮助。你们可以在l越来越多的人会选择使用AI来生成内容，但这不意味着我们要放弃创造力。我们可以利用AI的工具，但不要在认知上让步，创造出比我们自己或我们支持的团队更出色的作品，因为我们现在确实拥有更好的工具了。所以，请务必这样做。
